title: Early Cholas
capsule: The Early Cholas were one of the three principal Tamil kingdoms of Tamilakam, named alongside the Pandyas and Cheras in Ashokan pillar inscriptions of the third century BCE, with capitals at Urayur (modern Tiruchirapalli) and the port of Kaveripattinam. The most celebrated ruler, Karikala Chola (c. 1st–2nd century CE), defeated a combined Pandya-Chera force at the Battle of Venni and directed construction of the Grand Anicut dam across the Kaveri, an engineering feat that anchored Chola agricultural wealth. Another Chola king, Ellalan, ruled Sri Lanka from approximately 205 to 161 BCE before being defeated by Dutugamunu. The Early Chola line faded into obscurity around the third century CE, leaving a gap before the Medieval Chola resurgence under Vijayalaya after 848.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Early Cholas' territorial extent is poorly attested; the kingdom is known primarily from Sangam literature and epigraphy, and its boundaries at any given point are subject to scholarly debate.
